subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Refrigeration Cycles: Running Heat Backwards
description: A 60-second lesson on Refrigeration Cycles: Running Heat Backwards.

hook.text: A refrigerator moves heat from cold to hot. That's the opposite of natural flow — and it costs energy.

buildup.text: A compressor squeezes refrigerant gas, heating it. A condenser dumps that heat outside. The fluid cools and liquefies.

discovery.text: An expansion valve drops the pressure suddenly. The liquid chills rapidly, absorbing heat from the fridge interior.

twist.text: A heat pump is just a refrigerator in reverse. It pulls heat from cold outdoor air into your warm house.

climax.text: Air conditioners, freezers, and heat pumps all use the same reversed heat engine cycle.

punchline.text: Run a heat engine backwards. Now you can move heat uphill.

quiz.question: How does an expansion valve help cool the inside of a refrigerator?
options: It generates cold air by spinning a small turbine inside the fridge
It drops refrigerant pressure, causing rapid cooling that absorbs interior heat
It blocks warm air from entering through the refrigerator door seal
